summary: Optimizer calibration and safe demote plan for intermittent memory pressure after aggressive batching/quantization
description: Issue summary: Novara Labs began seeing intermittent pod OOM kills and multi-second tail latency on a handful of routes after enabling a combined optimizer bundle (async-batching aggressive, KV-prefetch enabled, and 4-bit quant profile). Impact: Production inference for two critical routes is degrading; customer reports ~15% request failures and elevated p95 latency. They are on Dedicated capacity with pinned model redwood-1.0-8B and a fallback to open-llama-3B-quant4x. Goal: provide immediate mitigations and a stepwise 'safe demote' plan to restore stability without data loss or config drift.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Tenant config: enable optimizer profile 'agg_async_v2' (batch_limit=512, async_window_ms=12), KV-prefetch=true, quant_profile=quant4x_aggr. 2) Send steady traffic at 60% of provisioned throughput with 95th percentile request sizes (prompt 1200 tokens). 3) Observe node memory usage and serving-runtime OOM logs. 4) Reproduce observed tail-latency spikes and 5xx failures within 20-30 minutes.

investigation_notes:
- Telemetry: node memory climbs steadily when async_window_ms > 10 and batch_limit > 256 for this workload. Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/tenant/novara
- Hypothesis 1: Combined KV-prefetch allocates additional per-request buffers that amplify memory usage under large async batches.
- Hypothesis 2: Quant4x allocation path has a peak working set not reclaimed between microbatches when async batching is aggressive.
- Reproduced in staging with identical config; memory delta ~+1.1GB per worker compared to conservative profile.
- Heap dumps and kernel OOM traces collected; next step is to provide controlled demotion steps and monitor metrics (memory RSS, page faults, GC cycles).

recommended_action_plan:
Immediate mitigations (safe, low-risk):
1) Snapshot current optimizer config: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/admin/tenants/novara/config/snapshot -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ops-token>'
2) Apply emergency soft-demote to the tenant (non-destructive): set batch_limit=128, async_window_ms=6, disable KV-prefetch for affected routes.
3) Keep quant_profile pinned but switch to 'quant4x-conservative' if available.
4) Gate changes with 10% shadow traffic for 30 minutes, then progressively 50% if stable.
Controlled rollback (if demote needed to be reverted later):
- Use snapshot restore endpoint with dry-run flag and verify diffs before commit.
- If rolling back quant changes, ensure to flush KV cache and restart workers on a rolling schedule to avoid transient double-allocations.
Observability & validation: monitor node RSS, pod OOM events, p95 latency, and error rate. Set alert thresholds: pod_memory_rss > 80% => auto-throttle to 30% traffic.
Follow-ups: schedule postmortem to assess quant allocation behavior and add an optimizer preflight test for combined KV-prefetch + async-batching profiles.
resolution: Partial mitigation applied: reduced batch_limit and async_window on affected routes and temporarily disabled KV-prefetch. Memory pressure subsided; OOM events ceased for 12h observation window. Planned next steps: engineering to run memory-profiling job for quant4x path (ENG-3247) and add preflight guard in optimizer rollout pipeline. Customer accepted workaround; ticket to be closed after 24h of stable metrics.
postmortem_and_actions: Action items: ENG-3247 (memory profile for quant4x under async-batching), DOCS-121 (add guidance for tenant capacity planning when using KV-prefetch), OPS-512 (implement auto-throttle trigger). Owner assignments: Devon Clark -> ENG-3247, Marina Ortega -> DOCS-121. Estimated ETA: 2 weeks for full engineering fix.
